finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts::`notesync.update` now opens a real yorkie `doc.update()` on every doc-changed viewupdate, including purely remote ones and re-entrantly during yorkie's own event publish
evidence: The mechanics are described correctly: note-sync.ts:61 calls store.batch() unconditionally on any docChanged ViewUpdate, and YorkieNoteStore.batch (yorkie-note-store.ts, batch()) always opens doc.update(), including re-entrantly during Yorkie's synchronous event publish. But the claimed defect doesn't materialize: an empty doc.update creates no change (context.hasChange() false), so nothing is pushed to the undo stack, the redo branch is not cleared, and no write/ops reach the server — contradicting "every incoming peer keystroke now opens a write transaction". The re-entrancy is precisely what notes-undo-integration.test.ts covers ("does not push the undo back as a new change" asserts depthAfterEdit-1 and doc.history.canRedo() === true; "applies a peer edit without recording a local undo unit" asserts the undo stack is unchanged), and the SDK's documented refusal is undo-during-update, not update-during-publish. The only genuine throw path (DocumentStatus.Removed) is a narrow edge since applyChangePack publishes remote-change events before applying the removed status. Confidence is medium because no checkout was available to read @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.13's Document.update/undo directly.
